latest.title: Kiro Specs: Deja de Improvisar y Empieza a Planificar Features con IA
latest.description:
Si alguna vez arrancaste a codear una feature "porque ya sabes lo que hay que hacer" y terminaste reescribiendo todo a mitad del camino... este post es para ti.
Kiro Specs es una de las funcionalidades más poderosas del IDE Kiro, y la mayoría de los devs la ignora porque suena a burocracia. Spoiler: no lo es. Es la diferencia entre vibe coding y desarrollo estructurado con IA.

latest.title: RAG and MCP in Agentic AI Systems on AWS: Architecture, Boundaries, and Reliability Implications
latest.description: The field is debating "RAG vs MCP" as if they are alternatives. They are not. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and MCP (Model Context Protocol) operate at different architectural layers in an agentic system and serve fundamentally different functions. Conflating them leads to architecture mistakes with direct production reliability consequences.

latest.title: AWS Bedrock AgentCore: Controls, Governance, and the Architectural Decisions That Shape Everything Else
latest.description: Once agents are running, the harder questions begin. This post covers the controls, governance, and architectural decisions that determine whether an enterprise agent platform operates safely at scale: Policy for deterministic tool enforcement, Guardrails for compliant model outputs, Memory, Observability, Registry, cost governance through Application Inference Profiles, and when a dedicated model gateway is worth the overhead. For practitioners building in production.

latest.title: Agentic AI for the Automotive Back Office: Where to Start
latest.description: 50–60% of automotive back-office work is manual. This guide provides a prescriptive framework for applying Agentic AI to cut costs by up to 3.78% of revenue

latest.title: AWS Builder Center: o guia completo para quem quer começar na nuvem
latest.description: A computação em nuvem passou de uma tendência para se consolidar como a base da tecnologia atual. A Amazon Web Services (AWS), a plataforma mais usada e completa do mundo, está no centro desta mudança. Com mais de 200 serviços em datacenters ao redor do mundo, a AWS permite que as empresas selecionem infraestrutura de TI de acordo com a demanda, pagando apenas pelo que gastam e evitando altos gastos fixos com aparelhos físicos. Mas como começar nesse mundo tão grande? A resposta está no AWS Builder Center.
